stem: Which of these must be present before a provision is recognised?

options.content: A present obligation arising from a past event
options.rationale: Correct: this is the first condition.

options.content: A decision by the board to spend money in the future
options.rationale: A plan alone is not an obligation.

options.content: A guarantee that the amount will be paid in cash
options.rationale: The outflow need only be probable.
The auditors do not approve provisions.

explanation: The conditions are a present obligation from a past event, a probable outflow and a reliable estimate.

stem: A court claim against a company is possible but not probable to succeed. How is it treated?

options.rationale: Correct: possible obligations are disclosed.
A provision needs a probable outflow.
It is not remote, so it is disclosed.
It is a possible loss, not a possible gain.

explanation: A possible (not probable) obligation is a contingent liability and is disclosed in a note.

stem: When may a contingent asset be recognised as an asset?

options.content: When its realisation is virtually certain
options.rationale: Correct: it is then no longer contingent.
A probable inflow is disclosed only.
A possible inflow is not even disclosed.
Optimism is not evidence.

explanation: Prudence requires that a gain be recognised only when it is virtually certain.

stem: A company sold 2,500 appliances with a one-year guarantee. It expects 3% to need repair at an average cost of US\$85. What provision should be recognised?

options.rationale: This assumes that every appliance needs repair.
The cost per repair has been left out.
The number of appliances has been ignored.

explanation: Expected repairs = 2,500 × 3% = 75 appliances; 75 × 85 = 6,375.
hints: Number sold × proportion needing repair × average cost.

stem: In December the board decided to close a branch in the following year but told nobody and prepared no detailed plan. What is recognised at the year end?

options.content: A provision for the full cost of the closure
options.rationale: A decision alone does not create an obligation.

options.content: No provision, because no obligation has been created
options.rationale: Correct: there is no valid expectation in those affected.

options.content: A provision for the future operating losses of the branch
options.rationale: Future operating losses are never provided for.
The closure is a cost, not a gain.

explanation: A restructuring provision requires a detailed formal plan and a valid expectation in those affected, for example by announcement.
hints: Has anyone been told, and is there a detailed plan?

stem: Which of these is NOT provided for under IAS 37?

options.content: Repairs under a guarantee for goods already sold
options.rationale: The sale is the past event, so a provision is needed.

options.content: Redundancy costs after an announced closure
options.rationale: A constructive obligation exists.

options.content: Operating losses expected in future years
options.rationale: Correct: there is no present obligation.

options.content: Damages that the court will probably award against the company
options.rationale: The obligation is probable and measurable.

explanation: Future operating losses do not arise from a past event, so no provision is made.
hints: Is there a past event creating an obligation?

stem: A provision of US\$8,200 was brought forward. During the year US\$6,900 of costs were charged against it. The provision needed at the year end is US\$7,400. What is charged to the statement of profit or loss for the year?

options.rationale: The balance left after the costs used has been ignored.
This is the part of the old provision that is left, not the charge.
The costs used have been added instead of deducting the balance left.

explanation: After using 6,900, 1,300 remains. To reach 7,400 a charge of 6,100 is needed.
hints: Remaining provision after the costs = opening - used.

stem: A company expects to pay US\$30,000 damages in a lawsuit that it will probably lose. Its insurer has confirmed that it will reimburse US\$12,000. How is this shown?

options.content: A US\$18,000 provision and no receivable
options.rationale: The provision and the reimbursement are not netted.

options.content: A provision of US\$12,000 for the uninsured part
options.rationale: The company is liable for the whole claim.

options.content: A US\$30,000 provision and a US\$12,000 receivable
options.rationale: Correct: the reimbursement is a separate asset when virtually certain.

options.content: A contingent liability of US\$30,000 only
options.rationale: The loss is probable, so a provision is needed.

explanation: The full obligation is provided for; a virtually certain reimbursement is recognised as a separate asset, not netted against the provision.
hints: Is the reimbursement certain, and may it be offset?

stem: A provision may be made for losses that the business expects to incur in future years of operation.
explanation: False. Future operating losses do not arise from a past event, so no provision is made.

stem: A contingent liability whose chance of occurring is remote is disclosed in a note.
explanation: False. If the chance is remote, nothing is recognised or disclosed.
hints: Disclosure is required unless the chance is remote.

stem: Match each situation to its treatment under IAS 37.

left.content: A court claim that the company will probably lose, reliably estimated
A claim that might succeed but is less than probable
A probable gain from a claim made by the company
A claim with only a remote chance of success

explanation: The treatment depends on the likelihood of an outflow or inflow and on whether the amount can be estimated.

stem: Complete the entry to record a provision for guarantee repairs.
explanation: The expense is charged to profit or loss and the provision is a liability.

stem: Name the standard that deals with provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets.

accepted.value: ias 37 provisions contingent liabilities and contingent assets

explanation: IAS 37 covers all three.

stem: A company sold 4,800 items with a six-month guarantee. Experience suggests that 2% will need repair at an average cost of US\$64. Calculate the provision to be recognised.

The balance on a provision at the start of the year was US\$5,300. Costs of US\$4,150 were charged against it. At the end of the year it must stand at US\$5,900. Calculate the charge to profit or loss for the year.
explanation: 5,300 - 4,150 = 1,150 left; 5,900 - 1,150 = 4,750 is charged. Taking only the change in the balance gives 600.
workedSolution: 1. 5,300 - 4,150 = 1,150 left; 5,900 - 1,150 = 4,750 is charged. Taking only the change in the balance gives 600.
hints: What is left of the old provision?

stem: A company will probably have to pay damages of US\$24,800. An insurer has confirmed in writing that it will reimburse US\$9,500, so the reimbursement is virtually certain. State the amount of the provision recognised in the statement of financial position.
explanation: The provision is the full 24,800; the 9,500 reimbursement is a separate asset. The net 15,300 is not used.
workedSolution: 1. The provision is the full 24,800; the 9,500 reimbursement is a separate asset. The net 15,300 is not used.
hints: The reimbursement is shown as a separate asset.

stem: State the three conditions that must be met before a provision is recognised.

points.description: A present obligation arising from a past event
A probable outflow of economic benefits and a reliable estimate of the amount

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There must be a present obligation from a past event, a probable outflow of economic benefits and a reliable estimate of the amount.

explanation: One mark for the obligation and one for probable outflow with a reliable estimate (both needed).

stem: Distinguish between a provision and a contingent liability.

points.description: A provision is a liability of uncertain timing or amount that is recognised because the outflow is probable and can be estimated
A contingent liability is a possible obligation, or a present one that is not probable or cannot be measured reliably
A provision is recorded in the statements; a contingent liability is only disclosed in a note

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A provision is recognised because an outflow is probable and measurable. A contingent liability is only possible, or cannot be measured, so it is not recognised and is disclosed in a note.

explanation: One mark each for the two definitions and the difference in treatment.
hints: Compare how probable the outflow is.

stem: Explain why a company may not make a provision for losses it expects to make in future years.

points.description: A provision needs a present obligation from a past event
Future operating losses depend on future events, so there is no obligation at the year end
Recognising them would create a liability that does not exist and would allow profit to be manipulated

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There is no present obligation arising from a past event for future operating losses. Recognising them would create a liability that does not exist and could be used to smooth profit.

explanation: One mark each for the missing obligation, the dependence on future events and the risk of manipulation.
hints: Which condition for a provision is missing?

stem: The directors of a company have a profitable year and wish to create a large provision for 'general business risks' so that next year's profit will look higher when it is released. Evaluate their proposal.

points.description: A general provision does not meet the conditions: there is no present obligation from a past event
Creating it would understate this year's profit and overstate next year's, which misleads users
IAS 37 forbids smoothing profit in this way; any existing obligations should be provided for, and risks may be described in the notes
Judgement: reject the proposal and provide only for obligations that exist

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A general provision for business risks does not meet the IAS 37 conditions, as no obligation exists. It would understate this year's profit and overstate next year's. The directors should provide only for real obligations and describe other risks in the notes.

explanation: One mark each for the missing conditions, the effect on profit, the rule and a judgement.
hints: What past event creates the obligation?

stem: Chitungwiza Appliances Ltd sold 3,000 fridges in 2025, each with a one-year guarantee. The company expects 2.5% to need repair at an average cost of US\$96. During 2026 repairs of US\$6,350 were charged against the provision. At 31 December 2026 the provision must be US\$7,800.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which account is debited when the provision is created?

options.rationale: That is the credit side.
No cash is paid when the provision is made.
Correct: the cost is charged to profit or loss.
The provision has no effect on share capital.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the charge to the statement of profit or loss for 2026.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the provision is a liability.

points.description: The sale of the fridges is a past event that created an obligation to repair them
An outflow is probable and the amount can be estimated from experience

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The sale created an obligation to repair faulty fridges. Repairs are probable and can be estimated, so a liability exists.

parts.explanation: One mark for the obligation and one for probable and measurable.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: State two effects of failing to make the provision in 2025.

points.description: Profit for 2025 would be overstated
Liabilities and equity (retained earnings) would be misstated, and the cost would fall into 2026

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Profit in 2025 would be overstated, and liabilities would be understated, with the cost falling in 2026.

explanation: This item tests a warranty provision and its adjustment.
hints: Only the increase needed is charged.

parts.stem: Explain why the closure of the branch gives rise to a provision although the branch is still open.

points.description: The announcement of a detailed plan created a valid expectation in the staff, a constructive obligation from a past event
The redundancy payments are probable and can be estimated

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The detailed announcement to staff created a constructive obligation. The redundancy payments are probable and measurable, so a provision is needed even though the branch has not yet closed.

points.description: A contingent asset is recognised only when realisation is virtually certain
Recognising a probable gain would breach prudence and overstate profit if the claim failed
They should disclose the claim in a note as a contingent asset, because the inflow is probable

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A contingent asset is recognised only when virtually certain. Recognising a probable gain would be imprudent and could overstate profit. The directors should disclose the claim in a note.
